Propose a batch of corrections from a filled template

Source: R/source_corrections.R
propose_corrections.Rd

Validates every row of a submission made from write_corrections_template() and returns a verdict per row:

Usage

propose_corrections(config, con, file, dry_run = TRUE, dialect = "mssql")

Arguments

config

A master_config from read_master_config(), with sources.

con

A DBI connection to the warehouse.

file

Character. The filled template, as CSV.

dry_run

If TRUE, the default, validate only.

dialect

"mssql" or "duckdb".

Value

Invisibly, a list: verdicts (a data frame of row, source, verdict), appended (an integer), correction_ids and file_sha256.

Details

  • appendable: the row passed every check below.

  • rule_not_fact: a key or the variable holds a pattern, a comparison, or "all".

  • unknown_source: the source is not declared in master.yml.

  • invalid_field: a flag is not 0 or 1 or disagrees with its value, the evidence type is unknown, or a required field is blank.

  • no_variable: the source has no such column, or the column is a key.

  • derived_variable: the column is the master's, derived from sources; correct the sources or change the derivation.

  • unknown_key: the key is incomplete, carries another source's key column, or matches no row.

  • ambiguous_key: the key matches more than one row.

  • does_not_cast: a value is not of the column's type, or the warehouse's cast to the column's SQL type would round, overflow or truncate it. This last check runs after the prior check.

  • prior_mismatch: the source no longer holds expected_prior.

  • duplicate_pending or duplicate_accepted: a correction already makes the same assertion (same source, key, variable, prior and new value) and is undecided, or its latest decision is to accept it. A proposed correction leaves the source unchanged until it is accepted, so without this check the same file submitted twice would be appended twice. An assertion whose correction was rejected or superseded may be proposed again.

  • duplicate_in_file: an earlier row of the same file makes the same assertion.

On SQL Server an append first takes an exclusive lock on each source's corrections, so two submissions made at once are checked against each other, not only against what was committed before both began.

With dry_run = FALSE, an all-appendable file is appended in one transaction, and a file with any other verdict is refused whole, with nothing written. Values are stored in a canonical text form, so "30.0" and "30" are the same assertion. A proposed correction applies only once accepted with decide_corrections().

Output is verdicts and counts, never a key or a value.

Interim. Superseded by the HVTR registry's intake, which takes over the template and the tables unchanged. Replaces the deprecated propose_correction().

See also

write_corrections_template(), decide_corrections()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("duckdb", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # Synthetic data; no PHI. One source view, its master, and a deployed corrections layer.
  con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
  DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "stg_demo", data.frame(mrn = c("SYN1", "SYN2"), lvef = c(30, NA)))
  DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "master_demo", data.frame(mrn = c("SYN1", "SYN2"), lvef = c(30, NA)))
  cfg_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".yml")
  writeLines(c("name: master_demo", "key: [mrn]", "snapshots: snaps",
               "current: x.sas7bdat", "build_program: x.sas",
               "sources:", "  stg_demo: {key: [mrn]}", "deciders: [dm_one]"), cfg_path)
  cfg <- read_master_config(cfg_path)
  sql_dir <- tempfile("sql-")
  dir.create(sql_dir)
  for (p in generate_corrections_sql(cfg, con, sql_dir, dialect = "duckdb")) {
    for (s in strsplit(paste(readLines(p), collapse = "\n"), "\nGO\n?")[[1]]) {
      DBI::dbExecute(con, s)
    }
  }

  # A correction to SYN1 and a fill-in for SYN2's missing value.
  sub <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
  utils::write.csv(data.frame(
    source = "stg_demo", mrn = c("SYN1", "SYN2"), variable = "lvef",
    expected_prior = c("30", ""), expected_prior_missing = c("0", "1"),
    new_value = c("35", "40"), new_value_missing = "0", evidence_type = "chart_review",
    evidence_ref = "invented note", asserted_by = "reviewer_a"
  ), sub, row.names = FALSE)
  propose_corrections(cfg, con, sub, dialect = "duckdb")$verdicts   # a dry run
  ids <- propose_corrections(cfg, con, sub, dry_run = FALSE,
                             dialect = "duckdb")$correction_ids

  # A named decider, not the asserter, accepts both; they apply on the next query.
  decide_corrections(cfg, con, data.frame(
    source = "stg_demo", correction_id = ids, decision = "accept", decided_by = "dm_one",
    reason = "chart confirms"
  ), dry_run = FALSE, dialect = "duckdb")
  DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM stg_demo_corrected ORDER BY mrn")

  # Upstream fills SYN2 with the same value: the fill-in is retired.
  DBI::dbExecute(con, "UPDATE stg_demo SET lvef = 40 WHERE mrn = 'SYN2'")
  retire_filled_corrections(cfg, con, "stg_demo", dry_run = FALSE, dialect = "duckdb")

  DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
  unlink(c(cfg_path, sub, sql_dir), recursive = TRUE)
}
